results.prompt:
Replace the viewport content with width=device-width, initial-scale=1 so users can zoom.

HTML:
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, user-scalable=no">
results.output:
## ✅ Fix Applied

**Replace this:**
```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, user-scalable=no">
```

**With this:**
```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
```

## Why This Matters

Disabling zoom (`user-scalable=no`) is a **high-priority accessibility violation** that prevents low-vision users from reading content. Removing this attribute:

- ✅ Allows users to pinch-to-zoom on mobile devices
- ✅ Complies with WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.4 (Resize Text, Level AA)
- ✅ Enables users with vision impairments to enlarge text up to 200%

## If You Were Disabling Zoom to Prevent iOS Input Zoom

If you added `user-scalable=no` to prevent iOS Safari from auto-zooming into form inputs, the correct solution is to set form input font sizes to **16px or larger** in your CSS:

```css
input[type="text"],
input[type="email"],
input[type="tel"],
input[type="password"],
input[type="number"],
input[type="search"],
select,
textarea {
  font-size: 1rem; /* 16px — iOS Safari won't auto-zoom */
}
```

This fixes the root cause without sacrificing accessibility.
